title: Why We Have Leaders
coreMove: Use rank as a burden-bearing function before claiming any privilege attached to it.
sourcePressure: Answers why groups need leaders: authority exists to preserve safety, trusted networks, and steadiness when strain rises, with burden before privilege.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Making leadership a title, charisma trait, or meal-time symbol instead of a protective function.

counterintuition: numbers versus people as a flat binary

exampleSpecs.stakes: crew need the captain to take burden before privilege
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain clips into the stern line first before sending anyone near the winch
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a wet winch drum under deck lights

exampleSpecs.stakes: guests and staff look for someone to preserve order

exampleSpecs.audience: dig leader after water truck delay
exampleSpecs.stakes: scarcity exposes whether rank eats first
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the leader fills student canteens before taking her own ration and explains the work plan after

exampleSpecs.audience: branch manager with an aggressive patron
